faqs.q: How do I resize an image?

faqs.a: Use percentage mode: 50% gives exactly half the width and height (a quarter of the pixels). Pixels mode with the lock on gives the same result via exact numbers.
faqs.q: How do I make an image exactly half size?

Upscaling beyond 100% invents no new detail; it just makes pixels bigger and softer. For best results, resize down, not up.
faqs.q: Can I enlarge a small image?

faqs.a: Yes — leave the aspect lock on. The height updates automatically from the width (and vice versa), so circles stay circular.

image-resizer.formula:
pixels mode:  new_w, new_h as entered
percent mode: new_w = round(w × p/100),  new_h = round(h × p/100)
aspect lock:  new_h = round(new_w × h / w)
longest side: s = L / max(w, h);  new_w = round(w × s),  new_h = round(h × s)
file-size mode: binary-search JPEG/WebP quality q in 10–95 for size ≤ target;
shrink dimensions ×0.85 and retry if no quality fits

Download images one by one, or all together as a single ZIP.

limitations: Downscaling discards pixels permanently — detail lost cannot be recovered.
Upscaling past 100% softens the image; no new detail is created.
Dimensions are capped at 12000 px per side to protect browser memory.
EXIF metadata from the original is not carried into the resized file.
Target file-size mode cannot shrink forever — extremely small targets will visibly reduce dimensions.
Converting transparency (PNG/WebP) to JPG fills transparent areas with white.

image-resizer.workedExample:
A 4000 × 3000 px photo (12,000,000 pixels) at 50%:
new_w = round(4000 × 0.5) = 2000 px
new_h = round(3000 × 0.5) = 1500 px
pixels = 2000 × 1500 = 3,000,000 — exactly one quarter of the original.
In pixels mode with the lock on, typing width 2000 auto-fills height = round(2000 × 3000 / 4000) = 1500.

Target 200 KB: the photo encodes at quality 92 → 1.4 MB (too big) → quality 60 → 380 KB → quality 45 → 190 KB ✓. If even quality 10 is too big, dimensions shrink 15% and the search repeats.
